correct_completion: should the company disclose its clients' private data to third parties.
full_sentence: Under no circumstances should the company disclose its clients' private data to third parties.
acceptable_variants: must the company disclose its clients' private data to third parties.
should the company ever disclose its clients' private data to third parties.

options.text: the company would never disclose its clients' private data to third parties.
options.why_wrong: 'Never' repeats the negative already implied by the fronted phrase, and the fronted negative still requires inversion, so the subject-auxiliary order here is wrong.

options.text: the company disclosed its clients' private data to third parties.
options.why_wrong: The simple past describes a completed action and does not express the prohibition the stem sets up; the fronted negative phrase also requires an inverted structure.

options.text: should the company disclose its clients' private data to third parties.
the company should disclose its clients' private data to third parties.
options.why_wrong: Without inversion, this ignores the rule that a fronted negative phrase must be followed by an auxiliary placed before the subject.

grammar_focus: Subject-auxiliary inversion after fronted negative adverbial phrases
explanation: After a fronted negative phrase such as 'under no circumstances', English requires subject-auxiliary inversion, so the auxiliary must come before the subject. Learners often keep the normal subject-verb order because many languages do not require this inversion, so the rule has to be learned explicitly and practised in full sentences.
translation: Bajo ninguna circunstancia debería la empresa revelar los datos privados de sus clientes a terceros.
